subject.title: Feature: Respect userTimezone in memory file timestamps and naming

question: Should bundled session-memory filenames and `# Session` headers use `agents.defaults.userTimezone` when it differs from the host timezone, or should that hook remain host-local while memory-core auto-flush uses `userTimezone`?
rationale: Current main has a source-proven split between auto-flush and session-memory behavior, and changing session-memory would alter shipped filenames/headers for users whose host and configured user timezone differ.

options.title: Adopt `userTimezone` for session-memory
options.body: Reuse the existing configured-timezone helpers, update the session-memory test/docs, and keep the fix within the current config surface.

options.title: Keep session-memory host-local
options.body: Document the split explicitly and close this request as a rejected product direction after maintainer confirmation.

options.title: Design a dedicated memory timezone setting
options.body: Open a broader config/API decision for memory artifact timezone behavior, accepting the extra config surface and migration burden.

recommendation.title: Adopt `userTimezone` for session-memory
recommendation.body: Reuse the existing configured-timezone helpers, update the session-memory test/docs, and keep the fix within the current config surface.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the merged host-local session-memory repair and is the clearest current-main routing candidate for deciding whether to revise that behavior.
